business_model.claim: The company is an internally managed hotel REIT that invests in upscale extended-stay and premium-branded select-service hotels. At the last 10-K date it owned 33 hotels with 5,021 rooms in 15 states and the District of Columbia.
quotes: The Company is internally-managed and invests primarily in upscale extended-stay and premium-branded select-service hotels.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 (structure) and P4 (TRS taxation); the consolidated-revenue point is inferred from the elimination statement
business_model.claim: The REIT does not run its hotels. It leases each hotel to a taxable REIT subsidiary lessee, and third-party managers operate them day to day. Lease revenue is eliminated in consolidation, so consolidated revenue is hotel-level operating revenue.
quotes: To maintain our qualification as a REIT, the Company cannot operate its hotels.

business_model.claim: The company reports no segment breakdown: it treats all hotels as one industry segment.
quotes: We evaluate all of our hotels as a single industry segment because all of our hotels have similar economic characteristics and provide similar services to similar types of customers.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A revenue table and text
business_model.claim: What it sells is mainly hotel rooms. In the third quarter, room revenue was $83,339 (table in thousands) of $90,921 (table in thousands) total revenue, or 91.7% of the total. The rest is food and beverage and other revenue such as parking and meeting rooms.
quotes: Since all of our hotels are select-service or limited-service hotels, room revenue is the primary revenue source

business_model.basis: stated in P1 for extended-stay and all-suite hotels only
business_model.claim: The customers described for its extended-stay and all-suite hotels are mainly business travelers: short-term transient guests and people on extended assignments or corporate relocations.
quotes: principal customer base includes business travelers, whether short-term transient travelers or those on extended assignments and corporate relocations

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q table; the inconsistency is noted from comparing the 10-Q text with the table
business_model.claim: Room revenue moves with occupancy and average daily rate, which together make RevPAR. In the third quarter, same-property RevPAR rose 8.3%. Occupancy was 83.0% against 79.1% a year earlier, and ADR was $194.45 against $188.58.
quotes: RevPAR, ADR and Occupancy are hotel industry measures commonly used to evaluate operating performance.

business_model.claim: Buying and selling hotels is a second revenue driver. A six-hotel portfolio acquired during the year contributed $7.2 million of third-quarter revenue, and total revenue was $90.9 million, up $12.5 million.
quotes: We acquired a portfolio of six hotels on March 3, 2026, which were located in Paducah, KY, Joplin, MO, and Effingham, IL.

business_model.claim: Disposals reduce revenue. The prior-year revenue decline was attributed mainly to selling seven hotels, with total revenue down $22.1 million to $295.1 million.
quotes: The decrease in total revenue primarily was related to the decrease in revenue from the sales of seven hotels

business_model.basis: stated in the income statement and the 10-Q MD&A
business_model.claim: The largest cost block is hotel operating expenses. They were 50,105 (table in thousands) of 76,538 (table in thousands) total operating expenses in the third quarter, and room expense was the largest line at 18,004 (table in thousands). The increase was attributed to the acquired hotels and inflation.
quotes: Room expenses, which are the most significant component of hotel operating expenses

business_model.basis: stated in P1 and the income statement; the rate shown applies only to the rows visible
business_model.claim: Some costs scale with revenue through fees. In the third quarter, franchise and marketing fees were 7,230 (table in thousands) and management fees paid to related parties were 3,064 (table in thousands). Base management fees are a percentage of gross room revenue, and the management table shows 3.0% and an incentive fee cap of 1.0% for the hotels listed.
quotes: Base management fees are calculated as a percentage of the hotel's gross room revenue.

business_model.claim: One related-party manager runs the whole portfolio. IHM, owned by the Chairman and CEO, managed all 33 hotels at the last 10-K date, so a large share of hotel operating costs and fees flows to an affiliate. The company lists this as a concentration and conflict-of-interest risk.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, IHM managed all 33 of our hotels.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items; the fixed-cost behaviour is inferred
business_model.claim: Below the hotel level, costs include depreciation (16,053, table in thousands), property taxes, ground rent and insurance (5,486, table in thousands), and interest expense (6,805, table in thousands) in the third quarter. Debt was $408.2 million at about 5.87%, and the term loan and revolver carry floating rates.
quotes: Interest expense on our term loan and revolving credit facility is based on floating interest rates.
As of September 30, 2026, we have total debt of $408.2 million at a weighted-average interest rate of approximately 5.87%.

business_model.basis: figures stated in P4 and P6; the operating-leverage explanation is inferred
business_model.claim: Revenue grew faster than hotel operating costs in the third quarter, which widened margins. Total revenue rose 16.0% and hotel operating expenses rose 13.8%. Management reported gross operating profit margin of 45 percent, up 110 basis points, and credits expense management.
quotes: through aggressive expense management, especially with regard to labor and productivity

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K; the caveat is inferred
business_model.claim: Demand is seasonal: the company expects lower revenue, operating income and cash flow in the first and fourth quarters and higher in the second and third.
quotes: Generally, we expect that we will have lower revenue, operating income and cash flow in the first and fourth quarters and higher revenue, operating income and cash flow in the second and third quarters.

business_model.basis: figures stated in F3; the funding link is inferred from timing and from P4's description of how acquisitions may be funded
business_model.claim: Cash from hotels funds distributions and part of growth. Nine-month operating cash flow was 67,812 (table in thousands), against distributions of 14,485 to common and 5,962 to preferred holders (table in thousands). Acquisitions of 92,458 (table in thousands) coincided with 100,000 (table in thousands) of revolver borrowings, and a REIT must pay out at least 90% of taxable income.
quotes: we must distribute at least 90% of our REIT taxable income

business_model.basis: stated in the earnings release market table
business_model.claim: Revenue is geographically concentrated. Silicon Valley hotels were 18% of last-twelve-month EBITDA, and their third-quarter RevPAR was $174, up 23%, so that market is a large swing factor.

competitive_position.claim: The company is a hotel REIT focused on upscale extended-stay and premium-branded select-service hotels. At the 2025 year-end it owned 33 hotels with 5,021 rooms in 15 states and the District of Columbia.
quotes: The Company is internally-managed and invests primarily in upscale extended-stay and premium-branded select-service hotels.

competitive_position.basis: figures stated in the cited items; the comparison with the industry is inferred from them
competitive_position.claim: In the latest quarter same-property RevPAR rose 8.3% on occupancy of 83.0% (79.1% a year earlier). U.S. industry RevPAR rose 7.1%, so the portfolio did somewhat better than the industry that quarter.
quotes: Smith Travel Research reported that U.S. lodging industry RevPAR increased 7.1% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, with RevPAR up 8.2% in July 2026, up 2.0% in August 2026 and up 11.0% in September 2026.

competitive_position.claim: Hotel margins widened in the latest quarter. Adjusted Hotel EBITDA margin rose 190 basis points to 39 percent and gross operating profit margin reached 45 percent. Management credits expense control, especially labor and productivity.
quotes: Adjusted Hotel EBITDA margins rose 190 basis points to 39 percent in the 2026 third quarter.

competitive_position.basis: figures stated; the lower-RevPAR comparison is inferred from two stated figures
competitive_position.claim: Acquisition is the main way the portfolio has grown. A six-hotel portfolio added $7.2 million of third-quarter revenue, and its RevPAR was $132, up 10 percent. The nine-month cash flow shows acquisition of hotel properties of 92,458 (table in thousands). The same-property set is now 39 hotels.
quotes: RevPAR for the recently acquired six-hotel portfolio jumped 10 percent to $132, easily besting underwriting expectations.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item; the concentration risk is inferred
competitive_position.claim: Performance is led by a few markets. Silicon Valley is 18% of last-twelve-month EBITDA and its RevPAR rose 23%. Some Northeast markets were flat to down in the same period, with Greater New York at (1)% and Coastal Northeast at (3)%. Management says Silicon Valley demand 'meaningfully increases EBITDA and FFO'.
quotes: Accelerating demand at our four Silicon Valley hotels meaningfully increases EBITDA and FFO.

competitive_position.claim: All 33 hotels were managed by one company, IHM, which is 100% owned by the Chairman and CEO. The filing names this concentration and the resulting conflicts of interest as threats.
quotes: The management of the hotels in our portfolio is currently concentrated in one hotel management company.
As of December 31, 2025, IHM managed all 33 of our hotels.

competitive_position.claim: The filing describes a highly competitive industry. Rivals include larger buyers with more resources, and competition for guests can lower occupancy, ADR and RevPAR.
quotes: The lodging industry is highly competitive.
Some of these entities have substantially greater financial and operational resources than we have or may be willing to use higher leverage.

competitive_position.basis: figures stated in the cited items; the link between borrowing and the acquisitions is inferred from the cash flow statement
competitive_position.claim: Leverage has risen to fund growth. The revolving credit facility went from zero to 65,000 (table in thousands). The leverage ratio was 23.2% against 20.1 percent at the 2025 year-end. Total debt is $408.2 million at about 5.87%. The term loan and revolver carry floating rates.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, we have total debt of $408.2 million at a weighted-average interest rate of approximately 5.87%.
Interest expense on our term loan and revolving credit facility is based on floating interest rates.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items; the persistence risk is inferred
competitive_position.claim: Lodging demand is cyclical, and the current industry strength may not last. The company lists cyclicality as a risk. Industry RevPAR fell 0.3% in the 2025 10-K year and rose 7.1% in the latest quarter.
quotes: The cyclical nature of the lodging industry may adversely affect the return on our investments.

competitive_position.claim: Reliance on franchise brands is a dependency. Franchisors can impose costly upgrades or cancel licenses, and the loss of a license can damage a hotel's value.
quotes: The loss of a franchise license could have a material adverse effect on the operations or the underlying value of the affected hotel because of the loss of associated name recognition, marketing support and centralized reservation systems provided by the franchisor.

competitive_position.claim: A development project is under way: the Home2 Portland, Maine hotel, carried at 4,540 (table in thousands) on the balance sheet. Management expects it to open in 2028. The filing lists development timing and cost risks.
quotes: Looking a bit further out on the timeline, our Home2 Portland, Maine development will open in 2028 and immediately be accretive.
Hotel development is subject to timing, cost, and other risks.

financial_health.basis: Balance sheet figures are stated in F1; the funding mechanism is inferred from the cash flow statement (F3).

financial_health.basis: Stated in P4 and P1; the cause of the rise is inferred from F1 and F3.

financial_health.basis: Figures are stated in F3; the quality reading is inferred.
